Yesterday I was browsing a subverse for sharing pictures. I noticed that some of the pictures were from sites without an encrypted connection and were being loaded, even though Voat is https and Firefox by default blocks mixed content. I checked with Wireshark and as I suspected, the TCP stream was not encrypted. So I discovered that Firefox only blocks active mixed content by default. In order to block all mixed content, you need to set security.mixed_content.block_display_content to true in about:config. For me this is a serious privacy concern, as I trusted my connection to be encrypted, while in reality I was downloading images any middle man can see (such as my ISP or whoever has access to it). I believe the default is as it is because this kind of "breaks" some websites. For instance, various images from various subs do not load when you expand them after changing the configs, since that would be mixed content. For me this is the desired behavior, however, as I want my connection to be strictly encrypted.

While using Wireshark I noticed something else, though. Firefox was constantly connecting to Google servers, even though I had all options concerning SafeBrowsing (which uses lists from Google) disabled. It also connected to several Mozilla servers. Turns out that there are numerous configurations which involve grabbing lists from Google and Mozilla. You can see them (and others) by searching url in about:config. I would suggest replacing all URLs you do not wish Firefox to connect to with a blank string. Aside from these configurations, this website has a few (very important) privacy related configs, such as disabling prefetching.

After doing the aforementioned changes, Firefox does not connect to any website I do not request it to (informally verified with Wireshark), and I don't see any more mixed content. Maybe this info is important to others, so I thought I'd share. I intend to compile a more detailed list of configs once I update my website.
